title: Laura P NDE 6698
content: For the past three days I had been taking a new medication prescribed by my cardiologist to control my heart arrhythmias. On the morning of the fourth day, I awoke with severe chest pains. My husband immediately called the paramedics, who quickly arrived within twenty minutes because we lived very close to their station. They put me in the ambulance and gave me something that would help me relax. Shortly after the medication, I fell asleep. At some point, I became aware that I was no longer here. I mean here in this world. And it was not a dream. I can't really explain it, but I was very much aware that I had entered into some other place. I felt an overwhelming feeling of love and an amazing sense of tranquility. I felt badly that I was leaving my husband behind with the kids in our cramped home in town, but somehow I knew he and the children would be all right. In the far distance, I saw a light. I could vaguely make out movement, as if there were several people in the distance. I could not make out whom they were. I was headed in the direction of the activity. I did not know how I was moving, but I was. Suddenly, I felt a crushing pain in my chest. My eyes opened. I found myself in the emergency room surrounded by medical personnel. The floor was covered with a long printout strip from the electrocardiogram machine. ‘Don’t do that again!’ I yelled. The doctor exclaimed, ‘She's back! She's back!’ I later learned that they had hit me with the paddles three separate times and then resorted to a cardiac thump, which finally broke the deadly rhythm my heart had fallen into. A ‘Cardiac Thump,’ or precordial thump is a blow to the mid-sternum with the medial portion of the physician's fist, from twelve inches above the patient's chest. It can generate five joules of electricity and restore a healthy heart rhythm. (From Wiki Answers).

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes 'Life threatening event, but not clinical death' I was taking a new medication to control my heart arrhythmias. The medication caused a cardiac arrest.
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: No I clearly left my body and existed outside it
elements.At what time during the experience were: Once I entered the other place, I was very aware of what was going on. Before that, I felt really ill with pain, dizziness, and nausea.
elements.The experience included: Tunnel | Unearthly light | A landscape or city | Strong emotional tone
elements.Did you pass into or through a tunnel?: Uncertain I haven't thought of it as a tunnel, but I guess you could say that is where I was.
elements.Did you see, or feel surrounded by, a br: A light clearly of mystical or other-worldly origin
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes There was light surrounding the images in the distance.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: A clearly mystical or unearthly realm It was dark where I was at, but there was an area of light in the distance with individuals and movement that I could not really make out.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: An amazing sense of tranquility and a deep feeling of love for my husband, kids, and family.
elements.God, Spiritual and Religion: point of no return? No God, Spiritual and Religion
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Christian- Protestant I was raised catholic but I am not practising
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience I experinced something that is consistent with my christian beliefs. I don't know why I did not see an angle or Christ but I figured that must have been because I was not there very long.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes I was having relationship problems. After that, I mended the problems and worked toward keeping good relationships.
elements.Concerning our Earthly lives other than: experience? God definitely exists Concerning our Earthly lives other than Religion
elements.During your experience, did you gain spe: Yes After the experience, I realized that my priorities had been all wrong. I had been working very hard for a nice home and life for the kids. I realized that material things do not matter. It is the love and relationships I have with my family and friends that matter. Everything else is just secondary fluff.
elements.Do you believe in an afterlife after you: An afterlife definitely exists Yes I felt like a I was seeing behind the "curtain" in the wizard of oz.
elements.Were you fearful living your life prior: Moderately fearful in living my earthly life
elements.Were you fearful living your life after: Not fearful in living my earthly life
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: Large changes in my life This experience had a massive impact on my life.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes Yes I cherish the relationships I have with others.
elements.After the NDE: tionships changed specifically because of your experience? Yes Yes I cherish the relationships I have with others. After the NDE
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes It was so amazing and unlike anything I had ever experienced. It took a few days before I told anyone what had happened.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience This was a very defining moment in my life that caused me to reevaluate my lives direction. I remember it very well.
elements.Have you ever shared this experience wit: Yes It was a couple of weeks before I told my husband what had happened.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Yes I had heard about it. I was not sure it was real.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real I have a friend who is a Seventh Day Adventist. He tried to convince me it was some kind of neurological episode. I told him that it was as real as going into a store I had never been into before.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real Very real. I do not doubt it happened. It changed my life.
